title: Finite constant-module tests detect etale Tor amplitude
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring, T a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and Q an object of D(T_et,A) [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let a,b be integers, with no nonemptiness assumption on [a,b]. Suppose that for every finite A-module M, writing M_T for its constant sheaf [def-kun-constant-sheaf], H^q(Q tensor_A^L M_T)=0 for every q<a or b<q [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Then Q has Tor amplitude [a,b] against every A-module sheaf on T_et [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

source.place: Closed-support paragraph, Tor interval assertion; detailed original node lem-sf-open-tor-bound-arbitrary-field, steps 4--6.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point t and write S for its module-valued stalk functor and C for S(Q) in D(A). The existing unbounded derived-stalk tensor comparison gives S(Q tensor^L F[0]) isomorphic to S(Q) tensor^L S(F[0]). Exactness gives S(H^q(-)) isomorphic to H^q(S(-)); mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor identifies S(F[0]) with S(F)[0]. Apply these to finite constant F=M_T. The module-valued constantSheafCompSheafFiberIso identifies S(M_T) with M A-linearly. Thus H^q(C tensor^L M[0]) vanishes outside [a,b] for every finite module M.

source.place: Tag 0DEN, clause (1), and Tag 07A4; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PT

proof.text: For any fixed C in D(A), choose a K-flat complex P representing it, using the source library exists_kFlat_iso. The canonical tensor-left counit and quotient tensor comparison identify H^q(C tensor^L N[0]), naturally in N, with H^q(P tensor N[0]). The degree-zero embedding preserves colimits, tensor with P preserves colimits, and filtered colimits of ordinary modules are exact. To formalize the last assertion, the colimit functor preserves short-complex homology by exactness; use ShortComplex.functorEquivalence to compare its homology with the colimit of the homologies, and then the homological-complex shortComplexFunctor. These comparisons prove that the displayed functor on N preserves small filtered colimits. This constructs the ordinary module tensor comparison directly for the existing monoidal derived tensor; it does not use the separately chosen mixed-tensor bifunctor of lem-pc-filtered-colimit-derived-tensor.

source.place: K-flat computation and exact filtered colimits, Tags 06Y6, 06YR and 00DB

proof.text: For any A-module N let I be the directed nonempty poset of its finitely generated submodules. Use Module.fgSystem and ModuleCat.directLimitIsColimit; Module.fgSystem.equiv identifies the colimit with N. Each submodule is finite by Module.Finite.of_fg and Module.finite_of_finite since A is finite. The functor in step 2 therefore sends every object of this diagram to zero by step 1. Preservation of this colimit and IsColimit.isZero_pt show that H^q(C tensor^L N[0]) is zero. This takes no direct-image colimit.

For an arbitrary sheaf F apply step 3 with N=S(F) at each algebraic-closure point of T. The comparison of step 1 gives zero stalks of H^q(Q tensor^L F[0]). The existing jointly faithful family of module-valued geometric stalks, exposed by sheafHom_ext_of_sheafFiber_map_algClosurePoint, then identifies its identity morphism with zero. IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero makes the sheaf zero. Varying F and q is exactly hasTorAmplitudeIn. The empty scheme, zero ring and empty interval require no extra hypotheses.

theorem open_tor_bound_stalk_filtered_extension
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (a b : ℤ) (Q : DerivedCategoryModule A T)
    (hfinite : ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} A), Finite M → ∀ (q : ℤ),
      q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero
        ((_root_.DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) q).obj
          (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) T).obj Q).obj
            ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
              (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) 0).obj
              ((constantSheaf T.smallEtaleTopology
                (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).obj M))))) :
    DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A T a b Q
